In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of scale in boilers is the result of a precipitation of insoluble salts of calcium and magnesium from water which has been concentrated by evaporation.
boiler scale is caused by the precipitation of the dissolved mineral matter in the water, which precipitation is brought about by heat and concentration of the water.

the scale in boilers is due to the deposition from solution by concentration of the dissolved mineral matter in water, the type of deposit being largely determined by the nature of the dissolved salts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chemical composition of the scale formed in a boiler depends upon the chemical nature of the water used and the temperature to which the water is heated.
the scale which is formed in the boilers of the various plants in this district is due principally to the presence in the water of the sulphates of magnesium and calcium.

the scale which is deposited in a steam boiler is a combination of the salts present in the feed water, together with those formed by chemical reaction between the feed water and the compound used to prevent the formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of a chemical compound to boiler feed water is not sufficient to prevent scale.
the addition of sodium hydroxide to a boiler feed water will reduce the scaling potential of that water.
we can use this knowledge to improve the efficiency of boiler water treatment.
